title: EU yacht pre-deposit document matrix
disclaimer: Orienting buyer checklist only — not legal, tax, or customs advice. National practice differs. Make completion conditional on matching documents before wiring a deposit.

vat_evidence.label: Strongest VAT / fiscal evidence seller shows

options.label: Original first-sale / dealer invoice with VAT line + payment trail
Import declaration (free circulation) + import VAT / duty receipt
T2L / T2LF (or equivalent Union-goods proof) only
Listing says “VAT paid” / broker letter — no primary docs
EU-resident buyer · boat already in EU waters
EU-resident buyer · boat outside EU / third-country flag path
Non-EU buyer · temporary admission / non-resident use
CE plate on hull + builder’s Declaration of Conformity (DoC)
Built before RCD / CE era for that hull (legacy craft)
No CE plate · no DoC · not clearly pre-directive

evidence_notes.title: “VAT paid” on a listing
evidence_notes.body: Market shorthand, not a legal category. Demand primary evidence matched to HIN / CIN and registry papers.

evidence_notes.title: T2L / T2LF
evidence_notes.body: Customs proof of Union-goods status after checks. Strong for free circulation; not automatically the same as a first-sale VAT invoice. Ask when customs may require Union status proof.

evidence_notes.title: CE / RCD 2013/53/EU
evidence_notes.body: Recreational craft 2.5–24 m placed on the Union market need CE marking and DoC. Non-EU builds without CE often need post-construction assessment before EU use — CapEx and delay risk.

scenarios.title: T2L on file, invoice archive thin
